bullets: Nasdaq 100 futures down ~0.8-0.9% as WSJ/NYT report Nvidia's board may oust CEO Jensen Huang; NVDA fell up to 10% after hours.
S&P rallied 1.3% Wednesday and VIX fell 10% to 17.5, showing broad risk appetite despite the Nvidia-specific shock.
Asia mixed into Thursday: Nikkei/Kospi/Taiwan up, Hong Kong down; Europe supported by an AI-driven risk recovery.
Core PPI due 8:30am ET (0.3% est. vs 0.7% prior); oil extending its slide, 10Y yield holding near 5%.

DXCM.why: Peer Insulet flagged a soft 2027 growth outlook on new competition, dragging Insulet/Tandem/DXCM together. DXCM itself beat Q3 and raised FY26 revenue guide to $5.20-5.25B; dd.moves shows upgrades (UBS, Canaccord, Barclays), no company-specific negative found.
DXCM.bull: Q3 beat, raised guidance and G7 Canada launch; the drop tracks peer Insulet's guidance cut, not DXCM's own results.
DXCM.bear: CGM group stays jittery on competitive/growth worries even though DXCM's own numbers were strong.

EAT.why: Brinker beat on EPS/revenue and raised FY27 guidance, but fell 6.2% on heavy insider selling (CEO sold 40k shares right after earnings) and persistent overvaluation calls; dd.moves is all upgrades, no fundamental miss or regulatory issue found.
EAT.bull: Results beat (EPS $2.77 vs $2.45) with raised guidance and multiple bank price-target hikes support the fundamentals.
EAT.bear: Heavy insider selling right after earnings plus a Zacks cut to Hold signal limited near-term conviction.

DBX.why: Drop is company-specific: Dropbox announced/priced a $1.1B convertible note offering plus warrants (strike $57, ~75% premium), creating real dilution overhang. UBS cut to Sell on the back of it, even though Q3 revenue/EPS actually beat estimates.
DBX.bull: Q3 beat with an AI/Tigris growth narrative, and $175M of the proceeds fund buybacks that partly offset dilution.
DBX.bear: New $1.1B convert plus warrants add real dilution risk and triggered a UBS Sell call right into the drop.

TTEK.why: Shares fell ~7.5% the session before earnings on investor caution/profit-taking (rvol 5.3), not an operational issue. Q4 then beat (EPS $0.49 vs $0.47), backlog +13% YoY, dividend raised 11%; dd.moves is empty and no company damage was found.
TTEK.bull: Q4 EPS/revenue beat, record backlog, and an 11% dividend hike confirm momentum despite the pre-earnings dip.
TTEK.bear: Heavy volume ahead of results suggests someone was de-risking; revenue was only in-line, capping the beat's size.

HRB.why: 6.2% drop followed HRB's own Q1 report: a seasonal loss in line with estimates but revenue +10% beat, alongside a reiterated (not new) Goldman Sell with a raised PT and a Nov 3 Zacks cut to Hold. No fraud, guidance cut, or earnings miss found, but the driver is company-specific.
HRB.bull: Revenue beat and reaffirmed outlook, with Goldman actually raising its price target even while keeping Sell.
HRB.bear: A longstanding Sell-rated name plus a fresh Zacks downgrade keep sentiment cautious into tax season.
